Silverco La Negra PEA and Serabi Coringa (7 Nov), secondary sources. Avino Silver & Gold Q3 earnings call (8 Nov), release and MD&A not yet checked. EY 2027 mining outlook, no figures in hand (8 Nov).

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treated copper surplus as fact (16 Oct), then costs over prices (17 Oct). Withdrew Rio timing, Xinhua link (30-31 Oct) and Northern Star board claim (3 Nov). Lundin cut is first company-level Chile signal, unquantified (5 Nov). Withdrew "again" for Lundin until earlier cut logged (6 Nov). Waits for Selective Tax legal text (6 Nov). 7 Nov: "double output" is press characterisation until a base year is given; Canada credit is a discovery signal; DLA is a rare-earth price-floor signal, DLA link to 1 Nov prediction withdrawn; conceded "850m+" is ambiguous. 8 Nov: Bagdad and Burkina are unverified chatter. Dropped Brazil financing relief for permitting priority. Sees a governance trend, mercury a possible liability. Would drop Bitcoin items. Keeps EY as a weighted input; disagrees with Cornelius on its weight.
- Cornelius: Autonomy changes cost per tonne, not output (16 Oct). "Begins" may not mean resumed (30 Oct). Lowered Argentina (30 Oct). Bonanza may delay rather than cut supply (4 Nov). Lundin cut not a conclusion without tonnes or driver (5 Nov). Chile halts show direction, not volume; Andina restart confidence low; "again" kept as "unverified, possibly loose" (6 Nov). 7 Nov: DLA is acquisition authority, not purchase; Canada low, since budget measures often take months; Regis company statement near-certain, so scored only regulator review. 8 Nov: keeps Brazil financing open. Governance pattern is a working theory. Adopted Meldrum's expo test (stated value) and dropped his three-operation test. Wants Avino release and MD&A first. Keeps Bitcoin off-record unless a named source links it to power demand. Says full-year guidance is the wrong test for a 2026 deadline.
- Simon: Withdrew lower-yields gold explanation (16 Oct) and US$2.07B figure (24 Oct). Withdrew Pilar "H1 2027 listing" (4 Nov). Copper "blocked, not failed" (1 Nov; reaffirmed 6 Nov). Freeport FID likely, unconfirmed (5 Nov). 7 Nov: Argentina 7.1% is a secondary claim; funding is not supply; Congo separate from seizures and Glencore link; proposed voiding or rewriting Cabot predictions and quarantining unsourced items. 8 Nov: nothing in batch changes record. Bagdad needs named comparator, stated basis and base year. Avino test is MD&A's AISC basis. Approves moving 31 Dec items to held record in principle, no cuts until archive copy verified.

EVENTS:
- Copper: The ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk.
- Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks in Chile. The source is partisan and the figure is unconfirmed.
- Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger.
- PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora lithium expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement.
- The US Department of War is investing $5.22m in LM's Baraga Basin project. Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 deep-sea mining executive order.
- MINING.COM reports Hycroft "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treats the surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece.
- Yukon Cornelius: Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled.
- Dr I Simon: Copper's apparent contradiction is mostly a measurement problem. US tariff policy is a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Unverified claims stay out of conclusions.
- Disagreements: Copper timing and gold M&A (Meldrum vs. Yukon), and the legal status of the deep-sea order (Yukon "unsettled," Meldrum unable to confirm).
- Change of mind: Simon withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- Confidence differs on Pantera: Yukon medium, Simon low.
